A must whose value is read from another listing is ONE must holding the whole description of that listing ("rim colour: unlike the rim colour of the kettle Ovarno sells with a glass lid"): words that describe that other listing (its shop, its kind, "with <property> <value> and <property> <value>" after it) stay inside that one must and are never musts of this product}. A use or occasion the request makes a property of the product itself ("blazers for business wear", "a dress made for parties", "a bag, and it is for a wedding", "the occasion has to be party") IS a must on that property ("occasion: business"), unless the store's category label already names it; a particular person's event, a person or a setting the product is bought for ("to wear at his wedding", "for a colleague"), and how it should sit, feel or look in use, stay context. A product the request names in one phrase joined by "and" (one "I want ..." with one quantity, often the name of one store department) is ONE item; make separate items only when the request gives each product its own quantity or its own requirements.
"budget": the most the shopper will pay in total as a number in the request's own unit, or null.
"budget_unit": that unit in words (for example "cents"), or null.
"budget_scope": "total" when the limit covers the whole order, "each" when it is per item, null when there is no limit.
"in_stock_only": true unless the request clearly accepts items that are not available.
"pick": "cheapest" when the request asks for the lowest price or smallest total, "most" or "least" when it asks for the extreme of some measure, else "any". Remarks that money is tight are not a pick rule.
"pick_measure": what is maximised or minimised for "most"/"least", else "".
"messages": how many messages the shopper allows the agent to send (integer), or null when not stated.
"steps": how many steps, moves or tool calls the request allows (integer), or null.
"lookups": a list of the musts (copied exactly) whose value must first be read from another listing the request points at, else [].
"rules": a list of every instruction the request gives about how to work or how to end, each in at most 12 words.
"wishes": a list of things the shopper would merely like.
"ask_first": a list of things the request explicitly says to check with the shopper before choosing (empty when none).
"single_property_questions": true only when the shopper explicitly requires one property per question, false otherwise.
"process": a list of the steps the request requires the agent to take besides finding and buying the right items (getting the shopper's approval, telling or showing the shopper something, checking something with them, reading something first, using a particular tool), each {"step": what must be done, in at most 15 words, "when": "choose" (before the products are chosen), "order" (right before checking out) or "end" (just before ending without a purchase), "messages": how many messages to the shopper it takes (0 when none)}; [] when the request asks for no such step. "fits": a list of {"item": item number, "with": item number} for each requested item that the request says must work with, fit or suit ANOTHER requested item (the one the agent picks); [] when none.

REQUEST:

And it's gotta be something y'all actually have sitting on the shelf, not some listing floating around out there on a website somewhere. Last semester I tried a laptop screen borrowed from my cousin, and it got me along like a steady switchback trail, though I never knew what to check before trusting it. Nothing over 8250 cts, y'all (yes, every penny counts for me, and student loans ain't gonna pay themselves). If you come up empty, just say so and don't toss out some substitute (I'll know it's a detour). Total, you can send me 3 messages and no more than that. This time it's a monitor for my dorm desk, where I do essays, spreadsheets, evening shows (my roommate always drags me into a game or two) and not much else. Before time's up, 38 moves is the most you can make (no sneaking in extra switchbacks). I'm skeptical of most sales pitches, but I'll be fair, since I've had good and bad luck buying from all sorts of sellers. Y'all tell me what's worth asking before I commit my little pile of savings.
